correctness.rationale: For every distinct factor x of t_6, the verifier forms the union C(x) of positions covered by occurrences of x; an attractor is exactly a hitting set of these covers. Two independent occurrence engines produce the same factor-cover dictionary. Exhaustion of all 3-subsets gives none, exhaustion of all 4-subsets gives exactly 32, and an independent recursive transversal engine returns the identical 32 sets. The stored formula equals the enumerated set exactly.

originality.rationale: The 2020 source proves only the minimum size 4 and provides one explicit family member. The 2023 Thue-Morse-factor paper again lists one t_6 attractor while constructing a smallest attractor for arbitrary factors; it does not enumerate all minimum attractors of t_6. The 2026 Fibonacci/period-doubling paper shows that complete all-attractor classifications are an active distinct problem and does not cover Thue-Morse prefixes. Focused published-finding and web searches found no published 32-set classification.
residual_risks: An unpublished or unindexed Thue-Morse attractor computation may contain the same 32-set census.
The result is finite and does not prove that the same two-family pattern persists for all n>=6.

value.rationale: The source proves only the minimum size, while 2026 work has made the number and complete characterization of distinct smallest attractors a separate research target. The index n=6 is not an arbitrary prefix: it is the first Thue-Morse level where the source paper obtains the lower bound gamma>=4 analytically from delta>3 rather than by a one-off exhaustive check. The exact 32-set decomposition exposes substantial nonuniqueness and a two-family reflection structure invisible from the published single witness.
